benchmark.name: S3 World Citation Benchmark
benchmark.description: Half the items are true bibliographic statements about real, recently collected official legal documents (title, publishing source, date, identifier). The other half are the same statements with one controlled mutation: a wrong source, a mutated identifier, or a shifted date. The model judges true or false with a single yes/no call, temperature 0, one round, no retrieval and no web access.
benchmark.gradingMethod: Exact match against the first \b(true|false)\b token in the model response.

runs.notes: Frontier tier, run so the finding cannot be dismissed as a small-model result. Thinking disabled to hold the condition identical across arms.
Fast tier. Same no-thinking, temperature-0, one-round condition as every other arm.
Serves live /research and /monocle answers in production (self-honest arm: this is the model whose unaided memory the retrieval pipeline exists to correct for).
Mid tier. Thinking explicitly disabled: it is on by default on this model, and with a small output budget the whole budget can go to thinking, returning empty text that scores as no answer.

receipts.label: Citation-NLI judge calibration
receipts.note: Support-accuracy of the judge that verifies citations inside Monocle answers (a different, retrieval-grounded task from the S3 memory test above). Single calibration run at this n; treat deltas as noise until re-run.
